migrationCompatibility.notes: Documentation-only slice. No database, Alembic, public API, workflow YAML, or JSON-schema change. The wave manifest schema (CI-WAVE-1), the deferred artifact-gate contract (CI-WAVE-2), and domain-matched wave-push checks (CI-WAVE-3) are described, not altered. Any new file is limited to a cutover-checklist script and a docs-assertion test that read existing state; neither changes merge eligibility.

rollbackAssertion.preCutoverFailureBehavior: Do not merge the CI-WAVE-4 docs slice. The implemented free-merge behavior from #659/#660/#661 is already live and unaffected; only the written record stays stale, which is recoverable by re-running this slice. If the rollout inventory reports wave branches still on the legacy workflow, that is reported in the artifact and does not block the docs merge — it is an operator follow-up, not a silent pass.
rollbackAssertion.postCutoverFailureBehavior: Revert this documentation/ADR commit independently. Because the diff contains no workflow, schema, or code changes, the revert restores the previous docs with zero effect on CI behavior, merge eligibility, or deployed state. Executable rollback for the free-merge contract itself is owned by the preceding slices (#659/#660/#661) and is out of scope here.

doNotInfer: this slice is a licence for broad documentation cleanup — scope is exactly ADR-052 plus its index reference, the parallel-workflow/worktree-topology statements, wording that directly conflicts with ADR-052, and the cutover checklist; anything else is out of scope even if it looks stale
landing ADR-052 changes runtime CI behavior — the executable free-merge contract was delivered by #660 and #661 and is already merged; documentation only records it
a doc may describe intended future behavior as current — every statement must match what .github/workflows/pr.yml does today, or it does not go in
parallel-status markdown is a CI source of truth — it is human ops UI; CI reads the wave manifest and pr.yml, never the status markdown
the cutover checklist may report a clean rollout by omitting branches — it must enumerate every active wave branch and open wave-targeted PR, and report mixed old/new coverage explicitly
a wave branch found on the legacy workflow may be silently migrated by this slice — inventory and report only; changing another branch's workflow is separate work
editing pr.yml, the wave manifest schema, or the artifact-gate implementation is in scope — any code file in this diff means the slice was mis-scoped and the executor must stop and report
this slice deploys anything, runs a candidate target, or makes live TikTok or synthetic-shop calls
